_note: Register: everyday standard Hausa, second person familiar (ka/ki mixed as context requires, defaulting masculine where a single form is needed, matching the pack's own convention) rather than the polite plural ku, since this is software chrome addressed to one user directly. Bare imperative verb stems on buttons (Fitarwa, Ajiye, Soke, Rufe) the way Hausa software UI conventionally does. Terms of art: a printed face is fuska and a sheet is takarda, so "faces/sheets" is fuska/takarda; duplex is ɓangarori biyu (two sides); typeface is nau'in rubutu; romanisation is rubutun Roman; the respelling field is Yadda ake fadinsa and the literal gloss Ainihin ma'ana; "glossed into" is An fassara zuwa. Romanisation systems keep their Latin/English names (ALA-LC, BGN/PCGN, ELOT 743, Hepburn, Hunterian, IAST, Kunrei-shiki, McCune-Reischauer, Okrand, Pinyin, RTGS) since Hausa has no settled calque for any of them, except roman.appendix-e and roman.rr, translated the way Indonesian's own catalogue translates the same two. Interpolation: Intl.DisplayNames hands Hausa a real language name already (Turanci, Larabci, Sinanci), not a bare ethnonym the way it hands Indonesian one, because the -anci/-nci suffix already means "language of" -- confirmed directly (Intl.DisplayNames(['ha']).of('ar') gives larabci, not just 'Larabawa') -- so no head-noun fix is needed on the {language} templates the way Indonesian's bahasa- prefix was. Interface-strings wave: a UI button is maɓalli / maɓallai (ha.wikipedia, Fasahar Maɗannin komfuta), not mabuɗi, which this file already spends on the pronunciation legend. Delete is Goge and remove-from-one-screen is Cire, leaving Share for clearing a list the way studio.balanceBlocked uses it; Settings is Saituttuka and browser is burauza, both taken from ha.wikipedia's own pages. Screen is allo / alluna, device na'ura, copy kwafi, voice murya. Confirmation prompts use the impersonal a rather than the ka the rest of the file addresses the reader with, so a deletion question does not sex the reader; explanatory prose keeps ka. komai, not kome. Hooked letters are written hooked -- buƙata, ƙarami, ɓangare, kuɗi, ƙasa, ƙafa -- and data/lang/ha/*.csv plus several older keys here still write them bare, which is a defect and not a house style. Interface-strings wave (studio, export, preview), printing terms: a tab stays Tab, the way this file already writes it at format.headSpan, because Hausa stationery has no name for the coloured projection on the edge of a card -- so that spelling is open to revision, not settled. Band and strip are ratsi (ha.wikipedia, Rawan dumi, "ratsi masu launi"); corner kusurwa, edge gefe, margin iyaka, each the word this file already spends on the same thing. "Rail" became a ratsi running down the outside and "fanned stack" became "tarin katunan ... idan an baje su kamar fanka", since Hausa has no trade term for either. format.headSlot.theme is Jigo, the word board.pickTopic already uses, because the slot prints the face's colour-group title rather than the name of the visual theme. .zip is written "fayil na ZIP" so a leading dot does not stand alone. gallery.tagline renders the product name Phraselet as katunan jimla, which is what gallery.docTitle calls it, and "tab your way through" as taɓa maɓalli. preview.lockDate and preview.lockTime are left out on purpose: they come from CLDR. format.theme.parchment is left out: Hausa has no attested word or loan for parchment as a writing material, and a compound built from fata (skin/hide) and rubutu (writing) would be a coinage without a source, the same risk this file avoids elsewhere.
